*Found one merge-blocking bug* in `share-editing`:

*P1 — Viewer shares can edit unlocked documents* — `src/guard.js:12`
`share.mask & WRITE === WRITE` is parsed as `share.mask & (WRITE === WRITE)`, so it checks the READ bit (`1`), not WRITE (`4`).

Confirmed:
• READ-only share, unlocked → `canEdit()` returns `true`.
• WRITE-only share, unlocked → returns `0` (denied).

Use `hasRight(share.mask, WRITE) && !share.locked`, or parenthesize the bitwise operation. Add regression tests for both cases; the existing editor test misses this because editors have both READ and WRITE.

All 6 existing tests pass. I also checked all 16 permission masks with locking on/off to confirm the issue. No other definite bugs found in the diff against `main`.

No code or files changed. I’d fix this before merging.

# notebin

Sharing permissions for notebin documents.

Each share stores its rights as a bit mask (src/rights.js): READ 1, COMMENT 2, WRITE 4, ADMIN 8. A viewer link has READ only. An editor has READ, COMMENT and WRITE. The owner has all four.

Check a right with hasRight(mask, right).

## Locking

> notebin@3.2.0 test
> node --test

✔ a viewer can view (0.645895ms)
✔ no rights, no view (0.126242ms)
✔ an editor can comment and edit an unlocked document (0.129377ms)
✔ nobody comments on or edits a locked document (0.126313ms)
✔ a switch turns a right on (0.592603ms)
